channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Arbitration – Military Lending Act – Cash advances
item.description: Where a putative class action under the Military Lending Act (MLA) has been brought against a defendant that offers cash advances, the defendant’s motion to compel arbitration should be denied because the text of the MLA demonstrates that Congress intended to preclude enforcement of arbitration agreements against servicemembers in disputes involving the extension of consumer credit.

item.title: Employment – Lie detector – Standing
item.description: Where a plaintiff who applied for three positions with the defendant was required to take a “Workstyle Assessment,” his complaint under the Massachusetts lie detector statute (G.L.c. 149, §19B) should not be dismissed, as he has plausibly pleaded that the “Workstyle Assessment” is a lie detector test and also has plausibly pleaded that he is a “person aggrieved” under the statute.

item.title: Jurisdiction – Forum selection clause – Clickwrap agreement
item.description: Where a defendant has filed a transfer motion based on a forum selection clause contained within the terms and conditions of a clickwrap agreement, that motion should be denied because the plaintiff was not given reasonable notice of the terms and conditions and therefore did not enter into an enforceable agreement with the defendant.

item.title: Real property – Trespass
item.description: Where summary judgment was awarded to plaintiffs who claimed trespass, a motion by the defendant to vacate that judgment should be denied despite her assertion that jurisdiction is lacking and that the plaintiffs no longer have standing now that they have sold their condominium unit.

item.title: Civil practice – Equitable attachment
item.description: Where a plaintiff has filed a motion seeking prejudgment security in the form of a $60 million equitable attachment, that motion should be denied because the plaintiff has not shown that it is entitled to any equitable attachment to enforce reach-and-apply rights under G.L.c. 214, §3(6).

item.title: Environmental – Wetlands
item.description: Where plaintiffs have requested a preliminary injunction, that request should be granted because the plaintiffs have established a likelihood of success on the merits of their claim that the “Notice of Intent” (NOI) and “Order of Conditions” (OOC) process required by 310 CMR 10.02(a)-(b) was not followed by the defendants.

item.title: Criminal – Murder

item.title: Securities – SEC civil enforcement action
item.description: Where a U.S. District Court judge issued four “obey-the-law” permanent injunctions, one of them must be vacated because it only cross-references the Code of Federal Regulations without any guidance for the defendant as to what his court-ordered obligations are.

item.title: Criminal – Health care fraud
item.description: Where a defendant was convicted of health care fraud under 18 U.S.C. §1347, his two convictions and his 27-month sentence should be upheld because he has not demonstrated any reversible error in the lower court’s evidentiary rulings, nor was it clear error to apply a two-level enhancement for abusing a position of trust.

item.title: Criminal – Contempt – Self-incrimination
item.description: Where a witness who was called by the government to testify in a criminal trial refused to do so, invoking her privilege against self-incrimination under the Fifth Amendment of the United States Constitution, it was not an abuse of discretion to hold her in criminal contempt when she continued to refuse to testify after being granted statutory immunity for her testimony.
